evidence.title: Blue light from light-emitting diodes elicits a dose-dependent suppression of melatonin in humans
evidence.text: Light suppresses melatonin in humans, with the strongest response occurring in the short-wavelength portion of the spectrum between 446 and 477 nm that appears blue.
evidence.context: Light suppresses melatonin in humans, with the strongest response occurring in the short-wavelength portion of the spectrum between 446 and 477 nm that appears blue. Blue monochromatic light has also been shown to be more effective than longer-wavelength light for enhancing alertness. We measured melatonin in 8 adults exposed to blue LEDs.

evidence.title: Exposure to room light before bedtime suppresses melatonin onset and shortens melatonin duration in humans
evidence.text: Exposure to room light before bedtime suppresses melatonin onset and shortens melatonin duration in humans.
evidence.context: Exposure to room light before bedtime suppresses melatonin onset and shortens melatonin duration in humans. In 116 healthy volunteers, exposure to room light before bedtime suppressed melatonin, resulting in a later melatonin onset in 99% of individuals.
